risks.title: Requirements split, or payments pitched just under a quote or approval boundary

likelihood.justification: The split-purchase test found {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.items}} supplier groups whose payments each stay under a boundary but together reach the band above within the test window, {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} of them in general procurement [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.counts.items] [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.general_procurement.items]. Threshold clustering found {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.items}} payments just under a boundary, {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} in general procurement [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.items] [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tag.general_procurement.items]. Both bear on the clause 6.16 anti-avoidance rule [rule:CPR-13] and the App B quote bands [rule:CPR-50] [rule:CPR-51].
likelihood.below_rubric_reason: The second test does not corroborate the first: at the quote threshold the band just under the boundary holds fewer payments than the comparison band below it (ratio {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[1].ratio_band_to_comparison|num}}) [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[1].ratio_band_to_comparison], and at the lower boundary the ratio is close to parity ({{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[0].ratio_band_to_comparison|num}}) [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[0].ratio_band_to_comparison], so there is no excess clustering. The split-purchase caveat also notes that regular instalments under one contract produce expected groups [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.caveats]. Rated Likely on the split-purchase indicator alone.

impact.justification: A requirement divided to stay under the App B quote and notice bands would bypass the three-quote and notice requirements [rule:CPR-51] [rule:CPR-52] and the clause 6.16 prohibition [rule:CPR-13]; groups at the higher boundaries would also bypass the App A board and Key Decision approvals [rule:CPR-48]. This is a reasonable possibility of challenge (Table 1 compliance, level 3). Contract Letting last received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-01].

evidence: Split-purchase groups: {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.items}} groups covering {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.distinct_payments}} distinct payments worth {{$.tests.split_purchases.gbp_total}}; general procurement {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} groups worth {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp]

At the quote threshold of {{$.rules_used.quote_threshold.value|gbp}}: {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[1].by_tag.general_procurement.items}} general-procurement groups worth {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[1].by_tag.general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[1].by_tag.general_procurement.items]

At the App A approval boundaries: {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[2].by_tag.general_procurement.items}} general-procurement groups at {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[2].boundary|gbp}} and {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[3].by_tag.general_procurement.items}} at {{$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[3].boundary|gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.counts.by_boundary[3].groups]

Largest group to examine: {{$.tests.split_purchases.top20[0].supplier_names}}, {{$.tests.split_purchases.top20[0].n}} payments totalling {{$.tests.split_purchases.top20[0].sum_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.top20[0].sum_gbp]

Threshold clustering: {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[1].in_band}} payments in the band just under {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[1].boundary|gbp}} against {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[1].comparison}} in the comparison band [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.by_boundary[1].in_band]
risks.proposed_focus: For the general-procurement split-purchase groups, starting with the quote-threshold and App A boundary groups, establish whether the payments relate to one requirement and, if so, whether the quote, notice and approval route matched the aggregated value (clause 6.16). Treat instalments under an existing contract as explained once the contract is seen.

risks.title: Contract and notice documentation to verify for high-value suppliers not matched in the notice export

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.non_placement}} non-placement suppliers above the publication threshold of {{$.rules_used.publication_threshold.value|gbp}} (annualised estimate of spend) could not be matched to a notice in the export [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.non_placement], {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} of them in general procurement [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.items]; {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.items}} suppliers in all [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.items]. The App B notice requirements apply above that value [rule:CPR-52] [rule:CPR-54]. The notice export covers only {{$.tests.off_contract.coverage.share_by_count|pct}} of high-value suppliers [metric:$.tests.off_contract.coverage.share_by_count], so an unmatched supplier is not evidence that a required notice is absent: it is an indicator that the contract and notice records need to be verified against the council's own documentation. The rating is kept at the rubric level because the unmatched spend reaches large general-procurement suppliers, where that verification matters most.

impact.justification: If verification found a contract at or above the App B notice band with no published notice or competitive quote process, it would fall short of the publication and three-quote requirements [rule:CPR-52] [rule:CPR-51], a reasonable possibility of challenge (Table 1 compliance, level 3). Spend above the procurement-legislation Threshold cannot be tested because that Threshold is not set in the rules extract [metric:$.rules_used.skipped_tiers[0].reason], so level 4 is not claimed.

evidence: Suppliers above the publication threshold with no notice match in the export (records to verify): annualised estimate {{$.tests.off_contract.annualised_gbp_total}} across {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.items}} suppliers; general procurement {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} suppliers with window spend {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp]

Coverage limit: {{$.tests.off_contract.coverage.exact_matched}} of {{$.tests.off_contract.coverage.high_value_suppliers}} high-value suppliers match a notice exactly [metric:$.tests.off_contract.coverage.exact_matched]; {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.with_candidates}} suppliers have near-miss name candidates for the auditor to check [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.with_candidates]

Supporting population: {{$.tests.high_value_suppliers.counts.items}} suppliers above the quote threshold on an annualised estimate, {{$.tests.high_value_suppliers.counts.notice_match.none}} with no notice match [metric:$.tests.high_value_suppliers.counts.notice_match.none]

Largest unmatched non-placement suppliers whose contract records to verify: {{$.tests.off_contract.top20[0].published_names}} (annualised estimate {{$.tests.off_contract.top20[0].annualised_gbp}}), {{$.tests.off_contract.top20[1].published_names}} (annualised estimate {{$.tests.off_contract.top20[1].annualised_gbp}}) and {{$.tests.off_contract.top20[2].published_names}} (annualised estimate {{$.tests.off_contract.top20[2].annualised_gbp}}) [metric:$.tests.off_contract.top20[0].annualised_gbp]
risks.proposed_focus: Documentation verification: request the council's contract register and, for the largest unmatched general-procurement suppliers, verify that a contract exists and obtain the procurement route and the published notice, or the recorded reason none was required (for example a framework call-off, a contract predating 2021, or a different legal or trading name). Treat an unmatched supplier as a record to verify, not as evidence that a notice is missing. Use results only for suppliers above the publication threshold; the test cannot speak to smaller suppliers.

risks.title: Payments to suppliers whose matched contract notices had all ended before the spend window

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.items}} suppliers were paid in the window although every exactly matched notice had ended before the window start [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.items], {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} of them in general procurement [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.general_procurement.items]. Extensions need the App C row D approval [rule:CPR-62]. A newer contract or approved extension without a notice may explain some items.

impact.justification: Continued spend on an expired contract without an approved extension would fall outside App C row D [rule:CPR-62] and, at these values, outside the App B quote and notice requirements [rule:CPR-51] [rule:CPR-52]: a reasonable possibility of challenge (Table 1 compliance, level 3).

evidence: Window spend with these suppliers: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.gbp_total}}; general procurement {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp]

Largest item to examine: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.top20[0].published_names}}, window spend {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.top20[0].window_gbp}}, latest matched notice end {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.top20[0].latest_end}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.top20[0].window_gbp]
Base of the test: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.suppliers_with_exact_match}} suppliers with an exact notice match [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.suppliers_with_exact_match]
risks.proposed_focus: For each flagged supplier, obtain the current contract or the approved extension (App C row D) covering the window payments, starting with the general-procurement suppliers.

risks.title: Spend-to-date against contract values and approved variations

likelihood.justification: As a screening indicator only: of {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.compared}} suppliers matched to one live single-supplier notice, {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.items}} have an annualised estimate of spend at or above {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.parameters.ratio_flag|num}} times the award value per year [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.items], {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} in general procurement [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.by_tag.general_procurement.items]. Variations need prior approval under App C row E [rule:CPR-63] [rule:CPR-64]. The analytics hold three months of spend only, so they cannot show spend-to-date over the contract life; award values may be estimates or maxima, and the annualised estimate is distorted by uneven payment timing [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.caveats]. The indicator selects the contracts for the spend-to-date comparison; it does not itself show spend above contract value.

impact.justification: If ledger spend-to-date exceeded the contract value with no approved variation, it would fall outside App C row E [rule:CPR-63] [rule:CPR-64]: a reasonable possibility of challenge (Table 1 compliance, level 3).

evidence: Screening indicator only: flagged window spend {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.gbp_total}}, annualised estimate {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.annualised_gbp_total}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.gbp_total]

Highest screening ratio, a contract to include in the spend-to-date comparison: {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.top20[0].published_names}}, ratio {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.top20[0].ratio|num}} of annualised estimate to award per year, against notice {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.top20[0].notice_id}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.top20[0].ratio]
risks.proposed_focus: For the flagged contracts (the general-procurement suppliers first), obtain ledger spend-to-date over the contract life from the finance system and compare it against the contract value plus any approved variations (App C row E), together with the variation approvals and evidence of whether the award value was an estimate, a maximum or covered other lots. The annualised three-month estimate is used only to select contracts for this comparison, not as the measure of spend against value.

risks.title: Repeat payments of the same amount to the same supplier within days

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.duplicates.counts.items}} chains of same-supplier, same-amount payments within the test gap were found [metric:$.tests.duplicates.counts.items], {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.items}} in general procurement [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.items]; cleaning also found {{$.tests.duplicates.counts.identical_rows_from_cleaning.rows}} rows identical in all six published columns [metric:$.tests.duplicates.counts.identical_rows_from_cleaning.rows]. Most chains are placements, where weekly rates produce expected repeats; the general-procurement chains remain.

impact.justification: The repeat value in general-procurement chains, {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp], is the amount at stake if the repeats were not valid. No CPR rule covers duplicate payment; this is a payment-control indicator. Accounts Payable last received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-11].

evidence: Repeat value across all chains {{$.tests.duplicates.gbp_total}}, of which placements {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.placement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.placement.gbp]

General-procurement chains to examine include {{$.tests.duplicates.top20[4].supplier_names}}, {{$.tests.duplicates.top20[4].n}} payments of {{$.tests.duplicates.top20[4].amount_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.top20[4].repeat_gbp]
risks.proposed_focus: Examine the general-procurement chains and the identical published rows against invoices and the accounts payable duplicate check; confirm whether each repeat is a distinct invoice or a recovered or reversed payment.

risks.title: Social care placements without a recorded reason for the choice of provider

likelihood.justification: Placement spend dominates several indicators: {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.mainly_placement}} mainly-placement suppliers above the publication threshold have no notice match [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.mainly_placement], with {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.placement.items}} split-purchase groups [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.placement.items], {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.placement.items}} repeat-payment chains [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.placement.items] and {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tag.placement.items}} near-boundary payments [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tag.placement.items] tagged placement. Placements are an App C row F exemption whose control is a recorded reason for the choice of provider [rule:CPR-65], so these indicators are expected and point only to that control.

impact.justification: A placement without the reasons recorded on the case notes would fall short of App C row F [rule:CPR-65]; with the exemption in place this is a low possibility of challenge (Table 1 compliance, level 2). Purchase of Residential and Nursing Care Provision last received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-14].

evidence: Placement-tagged spend in unmatched suppliers: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.placement.gbp}} window spend [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.placement.gbp]
risks.proposed_focus: Sample high-value placement suppliers and check that the case notes record the reasons for the choice of provider (App C row F), and that the placement rates paid match the agreed package.

changes.summary: Reframed as a contract and notice documentation verification risk: title, justifications, evidence and proposed focus now treat unmatched suppliers as records to verify, not evidence that notices are missing, given the limited export coverage. Scores unchanged (L3, I3); kept in scope.

Reframed so the audit test compares ledger spend-to-date against contract values and approved variations; the annualised three-month estimate is now stated as a screening indicator only, used to select contracts. Scores unchanged (L3, I3); kept in scope.
